title: A supported Koszul test controls low truncation of open localization
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover, and the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Use its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Perfect means etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $(i:U\hookrightarrow X,p:V\to X)$ be an elementary distinguished square: $U$ is a quasi-compact open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $p$ is representable etale, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, and $V\times_X Z\to Z$ is an isomorphism for the reduced closed subspace $Z$ of $X$ with underlying set $|X|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Put $T=U\times_XV$. There is a finite list $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$ with $T=\bigcup_{k=1}^rD(f_k)$. For every such list, let $B\in D(\mathcal O_V)$ be the associated etale complex of the Koszul complex $K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], placed in cohomological degrees $-r,\ldots,0$ by $B^{-n}=\widetilde {K_n}$ [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization]. Use canonical derived module functors [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] and standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Then $B_X=Rp_*B$ is perfect. For every $E\in C_X$, if $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(B_X,E[j])=0$ for all sufficiently negative integers $j$, there exists $a\in\mathbf Z$ such that the canonical open-adjunction unit induces an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$
$$\tau_{\le a}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\le a}Ri_*(i^*E).$$

source.place: Tag 0GFI, proposition-detecting-bounded-below, distinguished-square proof through the low-truncation comparison; supported transport: Tags 08HK lemma-pushforward-perfect and 08GG lemma-pushforward-with-support-in-open; affine orthogonality: perfect.tex Tag 0GEK lemma-orthogonal-koszul-second-variant.

proof.text: The open $U$ is quasi-separated: its absolute diagonal is the base change of the quasi-compact absolute diagonal of $X$. The affine $V$ is qcqs, so $T=U\times_XV$ is quasi-compact by the qcqs fibre-product lemma. Since $T$ is an open of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, refine it by the principal-open basis and take a finite subcover. This gives the required finite list, allowing the empty list when $T$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, proposition-detecting-bounded-below, paragraph Say V = Spec(A).

proof.text: Fix any such list. In degrees $-q$ the associated etale Koszul object has finite free terms with the exterior-subset bases; there are no terms outside $[-r,0]$. Indeed the affine associated etale functor is exact, sends $A$ to $\mathcal O_V$, and preserves finite direct sums. Thus this actual representative makes $B$ perfect. On $D(f_k)$ the operator $h(x)=f_k^{-1}e_k\wedge x$ has $dh+hd=\mathrm{id}$ by the contraction formula for the Koszul differential. It is a homotopy of the sheafified complex, and remains so on every etale chart of $D(f_k)$. Hence $B|_{D(f_k)}=0$ and $B|_T=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, Koszul construction; Tag 0663, Koszul contraction.

proof.text: Apply supported etale excision to $F=B$. It gives $p^*Rp_*B\cong B$ and $i^*Rp_*B=0$. The family $U\amalg V\to X$ is a surjective etale covering: it covers $U$, and $V$ is an isomorphism above the reduced complement. Both restrictions of $B_X=Rp_*B$ are perfect, by step 2 and the zero complex. Perfectness is defined locally on this site. For an etale object $W$ of $X$, cover it by $W\times_XU$ and $W\times_XV$. On the first, $B_X$ restricts to $0$. On the second, the derived isomorphism $B\cong p^*B_X$ from the strictly perfect complex $B$ is, after refining the covering, represented by chain maps by the strict-perfect local-actual lemma; these are quasi-isomorphisms because their images in the derived category are isomorphisms. So $B_X$ is perfect. Excision also gives, for every $j$, $\operatorname{Hom}(B_X,E[j])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,p^*E[j])$. Thus the assumed vanishing holds on the affine chart for all sufficiently negative $j$.

source.place: Tags 08GG and 08HK; Tag 0GFI, supported pushforward and Hom formula.

proof.text: Put $E_V=p^*E$, which has quasi-coherent cohomology by the etale chart calculus. Choose $a$ so that $\operatorname{Hom}(B,E_V[n])=0$ for every $n\leq a$; this is the same as $\operatorname{Hom}(B[-n],E_V)=0$. Use the derived etale/Zariski equivalence on $V$ and $T$. Its exactness identifies their standard truncations, and its canonical pullback and direct-image comparisons identify the open adjunction unit: both units are adjoint to the identity of the restricted object. The associated Koszul object corresponds to $C_f$, because etale realization is Zariski tilde followed by exact etale pullback. Apply the quantitative affine Koszul lemma to the corresponding Zariski object and transport back. For $k:T\hookrightarrow V$ this yields the canonical isomorphism $\tau_{\leq a}E_V\to\tau_{\leq a}Rk_*(E_V|_T)$. The comparison for $k$ applies because $T$ is a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme, hence $k$ is quasi-compact and separated.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, application of perfect-lemma-orthogonal-koszul-second-variant (Tag 0GEK); etale/Zariski comparison Tag 08H8.

proof.text: Let $u:E\to Ri_*i^*E$ be the specified unit. Etale base change identifies $p^*u$ with $E_V\to Rk_*(E_V|_T)$, and identifies $i^*u$ with the identity of $i^*E$; these are the canonical identifications respecting units in the chart calculus. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology and therefore with the standard truncation. Hence $\tau_{\leq a}u$ restricts to isomorphisms on $V$ by step 4 and on $U$ by the identity calculation. Its cone consequently has zero cohomology after restriction to the covering $U\amalg V$. Every section of any of these cohomology sheaves is locally zero on that cover and so is zero by the sheaf axiom. Thus the cone is acyclic, and $\tau_{\leq a}u$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 0GFI, check that the canonical map is an isomorphism after restricting to U and to V.
